description: OpenAI developer content source registry. developers.openai.com (the successor to platform.claude.com's old platform.openai.com/docs path -- that path now just 301-redirects here) serves a full sitemap and a .md variant of every page, verified by direct fetch. Output paths below are relative to content/openai/. learn.chatgpt.com (ChatGPT product docs, linked from the root llms.txt hub) is a known gap: a separate domain, not yet added.

developers.openai.com.notes: Migrated off platform.claude.com/docs in 2026; that path is now a redirect shell only. Single sitemap-index -> sitemap-0.xml, 1,321 URLs across api/ (726), cookbook/ (328), showcase/ (80), blog/ (36), ads/ (31), plugins/ (30), training/ (24), resources/ (16), learn/ (16), community/ (6), tracks/ (4), workspace-agents/ (3). Every page serves a .md variant by appending .md to the URL (after stripping the trailing slash sitemap URLs carry).

openai.com.notes: The marketing/news domain -- NOT developers.openai.com above. Model launches ("Introducing GPT-5", etc.) live here under /index/<slug>, in a sitemap category literally called "release" (https://openai.com/sitemap.xml/release/, 81 URLs). No .md variant (404) and no llms.txt (403). robots.txt allows crawling (Allow: /) but Cloudflare's bot-check blocks aiohttp near-deterministically (0/15 in testing) while curl with a plain browser User-Agent gets through ~50% of the time -- a client-signature check, not a real access denial. Scraped via curl + trafilatura, same as anthropic.com; see fetch_html_via_curl in fetcher.py. In one real run: 68/81 succeeded, 13 failed after 6 retries each -- self-healing across subsequent scheduled runs since a failed fetch is never tombstoned or reaped.

alignment.openai.com.notes: OpenAI Alignment blog. Static HTML, no Cloudflare (plain aiohttp gets 200). No sitemap/robots/llms.txt (all 404); homepage and /rss.xml both list posts and are unioned. No .md variant -- scraped via trafilatura like alignment.anthropic.com. Posts also link to openai.com /index/ and /safety/ pages, which are fetched too (curl, see openai.com) into openai/site/ or openai/news/; third-party citations (arxiv, LessWrong) are not.

deploymentsafety.openai.com.notes: Deployment Safety Hub: OpenAI's system cards (26 as of 2026-09-26). Sitemap lists ~1,060 URLs but on host http://localhost:4321 (build artifact) -- host is rewritten. Every /<card>/<section> URL serves the same full card as /<card>, so only first path segments are fetched. Trailing-slash URLs 308 to the slashless form.

model-spec.openai.com.notes: The OpenAI Model Spec. Root is a meta-refresh to the current dated version (/2026-08-18.html, ~2.6MB HTML); saved as model-spec/<date>.md so versions accumulate. Source repo github.com/openai/model_spec holds only the same HTML, so it adds nothing over the site.

sources.name: openai-docs
sources.notes: Full-site sitemap crawl, 1:1 URL-path-to-file mapping (mirrors claude.com/docs' approach). Covers API guides+reference, Codex, Cookbook, Ads, Plugins/Apps SDK, Workspace Agents, Agentic Commerce, dev blog, learning resources, showcase.

sources.name: openai-news
sources.notes: Model launch / release posts from openai.com (not developers.openai.com). Fetched via curl subprocess, not aiohttp -- see the openai.com domain entry above and fetch_html_via_curl in fetcher.py. Named news/ (not blog/, which is developers.openai.com's dev blog under openai/blog/) to keep the two domains' content visibly separate.

sources.name: openai-alignment
sources.notes: Alignment blog posts. Plus linked openai.com pages (output openai/news/ for /index/*, openai/site/ otherwise).

sources.name: openai-system-cards
sources.notes: One file per system card; see the deploymentsafety.openai.com domain entry.

sources.name: openai-model-spec
sources.notes: Current Model Spec version, filed by date.

notes_on_discovery: Verified by direct fetch 2026-09-17 (not yet wired into --discover, which is Anthropic-only tooling -- see fetcher.py). robots.txt points at sitemap-index.xml -> sitemap-0.xml; llms.txt is a hub linking out to per-product llms.txt indexes (api/, ads/, plugins/, workspace-agents/, codex/, commerce/, blog/, cookbook/, learn/, showcase/), each with its own llms-full.txt combined export. The sitemap already covers everything those indexes do, so the sitemap is used as the single discovery surface rather than crawling every sub-index.
